title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1969-01-24
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Sound Devices 744T -> Samplitude Professional v11.03 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a high‑energy 1969 Avalon show featuring a smoking New Potato Caboose bass solo and a stellar Dark Star.
ai_review.review: The recording, mastered by Charlie Miller, offers an impressively clear soundstage with only minor mix hiccups early in the set. Musically the night is a showcase – Phil Lesh’s unprecedented bass solo on New Potato Caboose, a soaring Dark Star, and rare moments like Pigpen on harp for Dupree’s Diamond Blues make it a standout 1969 performance.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high star ratings (mostly 5) and numerous detailed praises of both the musical performance and the soundboard quality lead to a strong combined score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Miller's remaster provides superb soundstage and clarity; occasional mix shift at ~1:11 makes vocals briefly recessed, and the vocal level is low in early sections, but overall the tape is crisp and well‑balanced.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Starts with a long tuning intro, moves into an explosive first set that builds to The Other One, then a tight second set highlighted by a 20‑minute Dark Star and extended jams; the pacing feels purposeful and energetic throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s Les Paul tone is praised; his vocals are occasionally buried early but come through strongly on Dark Star and later numbers. He also leads into Dupree's Diamond Blues with gusto.
band_member_comments.Phil: Multiple reviewers spotlight Phil’s extraordinary bass solo on New Potato Caboose, describing it as a rare, extended lead moment that drives the band.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s rhythm work is noted as solid; his vocal parts are sometimes low in the mix but he provides strong chord work on Dupree's Diamond Blues.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s keyboards are highlighted for tasteful placement and complementing the jams, especially during The Other One and Dark Star.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey Hart’s maracas and Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming are described as exceptional, particularly in the sparse Dark Star section.
